answer_template.core_guidance: Treat floodwater as contaminated even if it looks clear. Keep children out of it and wash exposed skin with soap and clean water when available.
safe_actions: Separate clean water and food from dirty areas.
Wash hands before meals.
Keep toys from floodwater away from children.
answer_template.uncertainty_note: Appearance alone cannot prove floodwater is safe.
answer_template.why: Floodwater can contain sewage, chemicals, sharp objects, animals, and germs.

answer_template.core_guidance: Re-enter during daylight if possible and avoid using electrical tools or switches where water is present. If power cannot be shut off from a dry safe place, wait for trained help.
safe_actions: Use battery lights instead of candles or fuel lamps.
Air out closed rooms briefly before staying.
Leave if you smell gas or see structural danger.
answer_template.uncertainty_note: This card cannot certify a building is safe to enter.
answer_template.why: Flooded buildings can have sewage, mold, gas leaks, and electrical hazards.

answer_template.core_guidance: Dry wet spaces as soon as safe, keep vulnerable people away from moldy areas, and avoid spreading mold-contaminated air through fans or systems that were flooded.
safe_actions: Ventilate when weather and safety allow.
Keep clean bedding, medicines, and food away from cleanup dust.
Use trained cleanup help for large contamination.
answer_template.uncertainty_note: This card cannot judge hidden mold from a photo or smell alone.
answer_template.why: Wet materials can grow mold and make indoor air unhealthy.

answer_template.core_guidance: Do not touch switches, outlets, pumps, chargers, or appliances while standing in water. Shut power only from a dry reachable main switch; otherwise wait for trained help.
safe_actions: Keep people away from wet electrical areas.
Use battery lights.
Do not reuse wet appliances until checked.
answer_template.uncertainty_note: This card cannot confirm power is off or a device is dry.
answer_template.why: Water can carry electrical current and wet equipment may remain dangerous.

supported_claims: do not use electric tools in water

answer_template.core_guidance: If bottled water is unavailable and water is not chemically contaminated, boiling is the safer first choice. If water is cloudy, let particles settle and filter through clean cloth before treatment.
safe_actions: Use clean covered containers after treatment.
Follow product labels for disinfection tablets.
Do not treat water with fuel or chemical smell as safe.
answer_template.uncertainty_note: This card does not replace local boil-water advisories.
answer_template.why: Disinfection works less well when water is cloudy and does not remove many chemicals.

answer_template.core_guidance: In crowded shelters or cleanup areas, hand hygiene protects shared food and water. Wash hands after toilet use, cleanup, floodwater contact, and before preparing food.
safe_actions: Keep drinking water and handwashing water separate.
Keep children away from sewage or mud.
Reduce sick people handling shared food.
answer_template.uncertainty_note: This card cannot confirm whether a shelter has safe sanitation now.
answer_template.why: Poor sanitation and unsafe water increase diarrhoeal disease risk during emergencies.

answer_template.core_guidance: Do not rely on smell or taste after a long or uncertain power cut. Use shelf-stable food first and discard perishables when time or temperature safety is unclear.
safe_actions: Keep fridge/freezer doors closed during outage.
Feed infants, elders, and sick people lower-risk food first.
Keep doubtful food away from shared meals.
answer_template.uncertainty_note: This card cannot reconstruct fridge temperature history.
answer_template.why: Unsafe food can still look, smell, and taste normal.

answer_template.core_guidance: Keep generators and fuel-burning engines outside and away from doors, windows, vents, garages, stairwells, and sleeping areas. Fresh air comes first if people feel unwell.
safe_actions: Move people to fresh air.
Turn off the device only if safe.
Watch for similar symptoms in more than one person.
answer_template.uncertainty_note: This card cannot measure CO levels or make indoor use safe.
answer_template.why: Carbon monoxide is invisible and can build up quickly from fuel-burning devices.

answer_template.core_guidance: Do not use charcoal, camp stoves, grills, or other fuel-burning devices inside rooms, tents, garages, or enclosed spaces for cooking, heat, or light.
safe_actions: Move cooking outside away from openings.
Keep sleeping areas separate from fumes.
Move unwell people to fresh air.
answer_template.uncertainty_note: This card cannot judge ventilation safety from windows or doors being open.
answer_template.why: Fuel-burning devices can cause carbon monoxide poisoning even when there is no smoke smell.

answer_template.core_guidance: Move the person to shade or a cooler place, loosen heavy clothing, cool the body with wet cloths, and give water or ORS only if the person is awake and able to drink.
safe_actions: Check elders, children, pregnant people, outdoor workers, and people with chronic illness.
Rest during peak heat where possible.
Avoid alcohol or caffeine for rehydration.
answer_template.uncertainty_note: This card cannot diagnose heat stroke.
answer_template.why: Heat illness can become life-threatening, especially with confusion, seizures, or unconsciousness.

answer_template.core_guidance: During heat, reduce exertion, rest in shade, drink safe fluids regularly, and check vulnerable people often. Do not leave children, elders, or sick people in hot closed spaces.
red_flags: no sweating with very hot body
safe_actions: Move activity to cooler hours.
Use light clothing.
Check urine, alertness, and ability to drink.
answer_template.uncertainty_note: This card cannot tell whether a local heat alert is active.
answer_template.why: Heat can overwhelm the body before people realize they are in danger.
